name: Thomas pulse (Cnp patent table, bilateral, 30 min)
origin: Alex W. Thomas and Michael A. Persinger (Lawson Health Research Institute / Laurentian University); the patent table (US 6,234,953: Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers, Persinger) as replayed in Persinger's lab
summary: The decelerating "Thomas pulse" as Persinger's lab replayed it: the exact 849-point table of US patent 6,234,953 at 3 ms per point, one 2.55-s burst of 18 pulses that slow down, repeated almost without a pause, on all eight temporal coils for 30 min. Saroka (2015) gives 30 min of this frequency-modulated pattern over both temporoparietal regions as the first phase of the lab's sensed-presence protocol.
notes: Changed after the primary-source check: this preset used to play the same table at 1 ms per point in the Lawson 4-burst analgesia cycle at 5 uT; it now plays the Laurentian replay (generator "thomas"). The patent's FIG. 2 is captioned "Thomas Pulse (Cnp)", so the Lawson Cnp and the lab's Thomas pattern are one table: the Lawson group played it at 1 ms per point (about 849 ms, around 100 uT in the patent's figure) and Persinger's lab at 3 ms, "849 points each programmed for 3 msec (each cycle lasts 2.55 s)" (Buckner 2015; Murugan 2013), with 3 ms between repeats (Murugan 2013; Carniello 2020). Within each cycle 18 pulses slow from about 12 to 5 per second; the lab's "25 Hz to 6 Hz" labels do not follow from the table and seem to describe its spectrum. Other lab texts give 839 or 859 points, and one rat study describes its frequency-modulated pattern as 837 values at 1 ms once every 4 s (Dixon & Persinger 2001). Saroka gives only "bilateral temporo-parietal", so all eight temporal coils (FT7, T7, CP5, TP7 and FT8, T8, CP6, TP8) play together, an inference; 1 uT is the lab's usual human intensity (cells and mice got 2-10 uT, Buckner 2015). persinger-saroka-2015-sensed-presence runs the whole two-phase protocol and lowfield-cnp-thomas-pulse the Lawson 1-ms version. Persinger's lab reported more left-sided sensed presences with the forward 3-ms pattern than with its reversal (Tiller & Persinger 2002), and in limbic-epileptic rats the 3-ms setting provoked the most seizures (Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999). Single-lab work. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, fear or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed or opaque goggles, in a dark, quiet room (the lab used a shielded acoustic chamber).
schedule: One 30-min session; in Saroka's protocol 30 min of burst-firing follow at once (persinger-saroka-2015-sensed-presence).
source: Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 and FIG. 2 "Thomas Pulse (Cnp)" https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Murugan 2013, MSc thesis, Laurentian University (849 points for the Thomas pulse at 3 ms, 3 ms between repeats; 248 points for burst-x) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/39c9c1ad-70ba-458d-a819-d24c20da217a ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, p. 89 (230-point burst-firing file, 3-ms points; Thomas file with 3-ms points and intervals) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Saroka 2015, doctoral thesis, Laurentian University, p. 29 (sensed-presence protocol: 30 min bilateral temporo-parietal frequency-modulated Thomas pattern, then 30 min BurstX) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/5260328f-a7c5-4d7b-b8a2-00b943eee977 ; Dixon & Persinger 2001, Int J Neurosci 108:87 (837 values at 1 ms once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11328704/ ; Tiller & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:26 (forward vs reversed 3-ms Thomas pattern) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11883572/ ; Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999 (3-ms points and intervals, limbic-epileptic rats) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10597585/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
